title: Introducing Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets, and Claude Data
summary: Whiteboards and Sheets launch in beta, and Dashboards become generally available as Claude Data, all included in paid plans. Whiteboards offer shared boards that can export to docs or decks and to Lucid, Miro, or Vani by Zoho, while Sheets adds tabs, formulas, formatting, drop-downs, logged edits, and .xlsx/CSV export. Claude Data adds certified metric queries, data stories, live sharing (beta), caching, and tracked changes with rollback, requires a data connector, and Enterprise defaults differ from Team plans.

title: Using Claude Opus 5.5 as your daily driver for knowledge work
summary: Anthropic recommends Opus 5.5 for everyday knowledge work such as research, analysis, memos, and decks, priced at $4/$20 per million tokens. It is now the default on Pro, Max, Ultra, and Team plans, with Medium effort as the default and thinking always on. In a merger-model test, Opus 5.5 Medium matched or beat Opus 5 High, finishing in 63 minutes versus 93 at half the cost.

title: Introducing Claude Meetings
summary: Claude Meetings (beta) lets Claude join video calls as a visible participant, answering questions by voice or chat, building docs and whiteboards, and writing notes and action items during the meeting. It is available on Team and Enterprise plans for Google Meet only, and excludes ZDR, HIPAA-ready, and CMEK orgs. Each meeting gets a claude.ai page with notes and transcript, transcripts are saved but not audio, and Claude stays out of calls with outside guests by default.

title: How Curative is building a national provider network with agents on Claude
summary: Health insurer Curative built a hierarchy of Claude agents, with an Opus-based agent named Gwen handling provider contract outreach through signature. The agents helped sign about 23,000 contracts at roughly 2,000-2,400 per week, versus 2,100 for all of 2025, and cut claims dispute responses from about 90 days to under 30 minutes. Its contracting team grew from 45 to about 55 with each member about 2.5x as productive, and its lessons include limiting agent authority at first, meeting providers on preferred channels (fax doubled win rate), isolating runs, and logging everything.

title: J. Crew brings its signature approach to styling to life with Claude
summary: J.Crew launched Style Advisor, an AI stylist on JCrew.com for US women's and men's shoppers that starts from an occasion or an item and returns full outfit looks drawn from J.Crew shoots, which customers can refine. It uses multiple Claude models: Fable 5.1 for planning, Opus 5.5 to prototype in Claude Code, Sonnet 5.5 for the stylist, and Haiku 5.5 for quick tasks. The customer story frames it as a shift from product search to an inspiration-led shopping experience.

title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which share the same underlying model: Fable is available to all users, while Mythos is limited to vetted cyber and biomedical organizations. The update brings better coding, reasoning, and vision, output up to 30% faster than 5.1, and an optional fast mode up to 2.5x faster at a higher price, with pricing of $8 per million input and $40 per million output tokens. Cyber and bio safeguards block about 55% fewer legitimate queries, and Anthropic self-reports that Fermat's Last Theorem was formalized in 30 hours with about 1,000 agents.
